brief: J.P. Morgan met 22 companies at Semicon Taiwan. Its central claim is that the leading edge foundry shortage worsens in 2027 rather than eases: unfulfilled N3 demand is close to 600k wafers in 2026 and widens next year because the NVDA Rubin and Vera ramp takes 55-60% of 2027 N3 wafers versus under 10% in 1H26, CPU programs from Google, Amazon and Microsoft all sit on N3, ASIC and networking attach add more, and TSMC adding about 40% N3 capacity does not close the gap. The same overflow pushes advanced packaging capex out from TSMC to the OSATs, with TSMC CoWoS at 190-200k wfpm by end-2027, leading OSATs near 100k wfpm, and SoIC becoming the 2028 focus as NVDA Feynman adopts 3DSoIC. CoPoS tracks slower, risk production 2028 and mass production 2029, while EMIB-T progresses. Test intensity shifts to Insertion 3 and 4 if TSMC skips CPO Insertion 2, which favours Chroma and Hon Precision. Logic TCB demand is strong, HBM TCB uncertain on the SK Hynix pause and despeccing. Top equipment picks are GPTC, Chroma, ASMPT and Hon Precision.
